title: delivery.json
description: The machine-readable definition of docs/PIPELINE-CONTRACT.md §1 — the agentic delivery pipeline's per-project config. This file and §1 are ONE definition in two renderings: scripts/check_schemas.py fails CI if a field exists in one and not the other. Shape lives here; semantics that a schema structurally cannot express (a UUID that actually resolves, a path that exists outside every worktree, perEffort vs the global cap) live in scripts/check_delivery_config.py. Neither replaces the other.
$comment: x-rule / x-tier / x-tier-<keyword> / x-fix are annotations read by scripts/check_delivery_config.py. x-tier says whether a violation is a §7 MUST-fail (error) or the advisory tier (warning); x-fix is the remediation prose a reader needs, which almost always lives in the contract's paragraphs rather than in the field name.
x-fix: Contract §1 defines the top-level sections exactly. Do not invent fields — a second shape for the same structure is what the contract exists to prevent; anything you learned that has no slot belongs in a report, not in this file.

version.x-fix: Set "version": 1. A reader that does not recognize the value must refuse to run rather than guess (§1) — and the PreToolUse hook classifies a version-less config as BROKEN and fails closed, blocking every tool call until a human repairs the file by hand.

teamKey.description: Ticket prefix, e.g. ENG in ENG-123. Uppercase.
teamKey.x-fix: Use the uppercase team key. It is lowercased for the branch name — the branch guard is [a-z0-9-] only — but the config carries the canonical form (§1).

workspace.x-fix: Set the workspace urlKey. Without it the dispatcher and comment poster cannot build a ticket URL (§1).

stateIds.description: The five workflow-state IDs. A closed, mandatory set.
stateIds.x-fix: States are referenced by ID, never by display name (§1) — a rename in the UI must not silently desync a guard. Run /setup-board to resolve the five UUIDs; a missing value stalls the whole queue.

working.description: A session holds it. Counts against budgets.wipLimit.

labels.x-fix: §1 requires an object with `ids` (canonical key → Linear label ID) and `required` (the subset that must resolve before the pipeline may dispatch).

ids.description: Canonical label key → Linear label ID. Values are BARE ID STRINGS, and ship as "" until a setup step resolves them.
ids.x-fix: Every value is a bare ID string — never an object, never a display name (§1 corollary, §6). Keys are the canonical names used in code; the Linear display name may drift from them. Run /setup-board to fill the IDs.

required.description: Subset of labels.ids keys that must resolve before the pipeline may dispatch.
required.x-fix: An array of canonical label keys from §6. Every entry must have an entry in labels.ids that resolves to a real ID — guards compare IDs, never display names (§1, §6).

github.x-fix: §1 requires owner, repo and defaultBranch — the last is the base for PRs and the ref guards read config values from.

defaultBranch.description: Base for PRs and the ref guards read config values from. Default main.

types.description: Allowed branch type prefixes. Must stay a subset of what the live PreToolUse branch-naming guard accepts.
types.x-fix: A session on a branch the live guard rejects is blocked before its first edit (§1, §7). The enum here, the fallback list in scripts/check_delivery_config.py and the live guard's own regex are asserted equal by that script's selftest — widen one and CI names the other two.

requireTicketId.description: When true, the slug must begin with the ticket ID, lowercased.
requireTicketId.x-fix: §1 defines a boolean. The `ticket-branch` guard is scoped to it being true (§2).

kind.description: Stack identifier used to pick command defaults and prompt fragments, e.g. node-ts, python, go, mixed.

securityNotes.description: Stack-specific cautions injected into session and review prompts. Prompt material, never a guard.

graderPaths.description: Globs a reviewer must always inspect. Advisory; distinct from autonomy.riskPaths, which is enforced.

commands.description: The local gate. An absent key and null both mean 'no such step' and a runner skips it.
commands.x-fix: §1: null is how a project says it has no such step. An empty string is invalid — it hides a misconfiguration behind a no-op, and the runner reports a step it never ran.

preview.description: Starts the app for a human/visual check.

perEffort.description: Selected by the ticket's effort:* label.

maxTurns.description: Hard ceiling. Effective turns = min(perEffort[e].maxTurns, maxTurns).
maxTurns.x-fix: §1 requires the hard turn ceiling as an integer ≥ 1. The §7 per-effort rule cannot be evaluated without it.

wipLimit.description: Max tickets in `working` at once, across the whole team.

maxBounces.description: Max review→fix round trips on one ticket before agent:needs-human. One bounce = one fix session, counted out of session (§9). The enforced one.

fixIterations.description: Max read→fix→push→re-watch cycles INSIDE one fix session. Prompt material, not a guard.
fixIterations.x-fix: §1 requires an integer ≥ 1 (default 3, matching /fix-ci's own bound). It is a different number from budgets.maxBounces, which bounds how many fix sessions the pipeline pays for — reusing one value for both couples them at exactly the wrong place.

totalAttempts.description: Max dispatches of one ticket across all stages and bounces. The count lives in the dispatcher state record (§9).

dailyUsd.description: Rolling 24h spend cap for the whole pipeline, metered by the dispatcher — never by a session's self-reported cost.

reviewSeverityThreshold.description: Lowest review severity that blocks progress and starts a bounce. Findings below it are posted as comments only.

auth.description: Which credential each context uses, so cost attribution and rate-limit blast radius are predictable.
auth.x-fix: §1 defines subscription|api-key for every context, and §7 fails anything else. Unattended lanes are normally kept off the interactive credential so a runaway queue cannot exhaust a human's session capacity.

autoApproveProvenance.description: Provenance classes allowed to move raw → ready without a human. Must be a subset of ["epic"].
autoApproveProvenance.x-fix: §5 rule 3, §7: only epic/* may auto-approve, because nothing an agent files carries epic provenance. Widening this lets an agent widen its own mandate by filing tickets for itself. An empty array is a valid subset — it means nothing auto-approves.

autoMergeMaxLines.description: Diff-size ceiling under which an OUT-OF-SESSION automation may merge. 0 disables. No Claude Code session may ever act on this — the merge command is hook-blocked in every form, including --auto.

autoMergeMethod.description: Optional. How the platform merges a qualifying PR. Default squash. Cosmetic — it decides nothing about WHETHER a PR merges.

riskPaths.description: Globs that force human review regardless of diff size or provenance. Enforced, unlike stack.graderPaths.
riskPaths.x-fix: §1/§7: the guard machinery and delivery.json always need a human — a PR that edits supervision is not a routine edit. The required floor is checked as an exact glob string by scripts/check_delivery_config.py.

backend.description: Where sessions run. An unknown backend has no declared durable store, so statePath is treated as required (§9).

labelTrigger.description: Canonical label key (resolved through linear.labels.ids) whose presence queues a ticket. Default agent:queued.

pauseOnCapacity.description: On a provider capacity error, pause the queue and apply blocked:capacity instead of consuming a totalAttempts slot.

pinsRoot.description: Directory for pin files. Default ~/.claude/pipeline/pins. Must resolve OUTSIDE the repo and every worktree.
pinsRoot.x-fix: §1, §3: the pin is the only authority binding a session to its ticket, and a pin the session can write is not a pin. Use ~/.claude/pipeline/pins. Pins are short-lived — nothing durable may be stored there (§9).

statePath.description: Where the dispatcher state record (§9) is kept. null when the backend supplies its own durable store — github-actions, where the store is the pipeline-state artifact.
statePath.x-fix: §1 requires the key: a path outside the repo and every worktree, or null for a backend with its own durable store. §9: a counter the agent can edit is not a counter.

stormPerHour.description: Max alerts emitted per hour; beyond it, alerts are coalesced. Stops one broken cron filing a hundred tickets.

telemetry.description: OPTIONAL. Absent ⇒ collection is off: the collector exits 0 and emits nothing. Deliberately NOT judged by the §7 validator — every §7 row gates autonomy, and telemetry gates nothing. Its consumer, scripts/telemetry_scrape.py, validates it at the point of use.

store.description: A collector that does not recognize the value refuses to run rather than guessing at a dialect.

dsnEnv.description: The NAME of an environment variable holding the connection string — never the connection string. A DSN carries a password and delivery.json is a tracked file.

schema.description: SQL schema the tables live in. Default pipeline. Must be a plain identifier — it is interpolated into SQL, so a placeholder token is not acceptable here even in the shipped example.

lookbackDays.description: How far back a sweep reads. Default 30; the sweep is idempotent (§10), so overlap is free and a gap is not.

maxTurns.x-fix: §1, §7: effective turns = min(perEffort[e].maxTurns, budgets.maxTurns) — a per-effort value may only LOWER the cap, never raise it.
